concepts.name: Image versus container
concepts.summary: Explain that an image is a read-only packaged template and a container is a running (or stopped) instance created from it.

concepts.name: Pulling and listing images
concepts.summary: Recall how to fetch an image from a registry by name and tag and list local images.

concepts.name: Running a container
concepts.summary: Understand that docker run creates and starts a container from an image and runs its default command.

concepts.name: Container lifecycle commands
concepts.summary: Remember the commands to list, stop, start and remove containers and distinguish running from stopped ones.

concepts.name: Image tags
concepts.summary: Understand that a tag labels a version of an image in the form repository:tag and that omitting it defaults to latest.

concepts.name: Dockerfile as build recipe
concepts.summary: Understand that a Dockerfile is a text file of instructions from which docker build produces an image.

misconceptions.text: A container is a full virtual machine with its own kernel.
The latest tag always points to the newest version of an image.

concepts.name: Core Dockerfile instructions
concepts.summary: Write a Dockerfile using FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN and EXPOSE to package a simple application.

concepts.name: CMD versus ENTRYPOINT
concepts.summary: Apply CMD for overridable default commands and ENTRYPOINT for the fixed executable, and predict how arguments to docker run combine with them.

concepts.name: Building and tagging images
concepts.summary: Run docker build with a tag and build context to produce a named image.

concepts.name: Port mapping
concepts.summary: Use -p host:container to make a containerized service reachable from the host.

concepts.name: Environment variables and run options
concepts.summary: Use flags to run detached, name containers, remove on exit and pass environment variables.

concepts.name: Bind mounts and volumes
concepts.summary: Persist or share data by mounting a host directory or a named volume into a container.

concepts.name: Logs and exec inspection
concepts.summary: Use docker logs and docker exec to see output and run commands inside a running container.

misconceptions.text: Data written inside a container persists after the container is removed.
EXPOSE in a Dockerfile publishes the port to the host.
CMD and ENTRYPOINT are interchangeable and behave the same.

concepts.name: Layers and build cache
concepts.summary: Analyse how each instruction creates a layer and how cache invalidation propagates to later layers, then order instructions to maximise reuse.

concepts.name: Multi-stage builds
concepts.summary: Separate build and runtime stages so only needed artifacts are copied into a small final image.

concepts.name: Bridge networks and name resolution
concepts.summary: Explain how containers on a user-defined bridge network reach each other by name and how this differs from the default bridge.

concepts.name: Compose service definitions
concepts.summary: Describe multi-container applications in a compose file with image or build, ports, environment, volumes and depends_on.

concepts.name: Compose lifecycle commands
concepts.summary: Start, stop, rebuild and tear down a compose project, including removing volumes deliberately.

concepts.name: Dockerignore and context size
concepts.summary: Exclude unneeded files from the build context to speed builds and avoid leaking files into images.

concepts.name: Publishing to Docker Hub
concepts.summary: Log in, tag an image with a repository name and push it to Docker Hub so others can pull it.

concepts.name: Debugging failing containers
concepts.summary: Diagnose crashes using logs, exit codes, inspect output and interactive shells.

misconceptions.text: depends_on guarantees the dependency service is ready to accept connections.
Deleting a file in a later RUN layer shrinks the image.
Containers must use localhost to reach other containers on the same network.

concepts.name: Image size and layer optimisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate base image choices and layer strategies to trade off size, build speed and debuggability.

concepts.name: Secrets and configuration handling
concepts.summary: Judge where configuration belongs among ARG, ENV, env files and secrets, and avoid baking credentials into layers.

concepts.name: Non-root and least privilege
concepts.summary: Assess and reduce risk by running as a non-root user, dropping capabilities and using read-only filesystems.

concepts.name: Health checks and restart policies
concepts.summary: Analyse how health checks and restart policies affect availability and startup ordering in compose.

concepts.name: Compose environments and overrides
concepts.summary: Structure compose files with overrides, profiles and variable substitution for dev and production differences.

concepts.name: Signal handling and PID 1
concepts.summary: Explain why exec-form commands and init handling matter for receiving SIGTERM and shutting down cleanly.

concepts.name: Tagging and versioning strategy
concepts.summary: Evaluate tagging schemes and digest pinning for reproducibility and safe rollbacks.

misconceptions.text: Secrets passed with ARG or deleted in a later layer are safe from image inspection.
Processes in containers run as an unprivileged user by default.
Shell-form CMD handles SIGTERM just as well as exec form.

concepts.name: Reproducible and cacheable CI builds
concepts.summary: Design build pipelines with cache mounts, remote cache and pinned inputs for fast, deterministic images.

concepts.name: Supply chain integrity
concepts.summary: Evaluate provenance, scanning, signing and base image trust policies for images entering production.

concepts.name: Multi-architecture images
concepts.summary: Create images that run on several CPU architectures using multi-platform builds and manifests.

concepts.name: Isolation internals
concepts.summary: Evaluate the guarantees and limits of container isolation based on namespaces, cgroups and shared kernel, and set resource limits accordingly.

concepts.name: Storage and network driver trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge when to use volumes, tmpfs, host or macvlan networking and understand copy-on-write storage costs.

concepts.name: Container platform design standards
concepts.summary: Create team standards and templated Dockerfiles and compose setups that balance security, size and developer experience.

concepts.name: Moving beyond single-host Docker
concepts.summary: Evaluate when compose on one host stops being sufficient and what must change to move to an orchestrator.

misconceptions.text: Containers provide the same isolation strength as virtual machines.
Scanning an image once at build time keeps it secure over its lifetime.
An image built on one CPU architecture runs unchanged on any other.
